decisions.reason: The polymer concrete housing has its own page and supports the firm's integrated drainage families, so the visible investment and strategic fit favor persisting.
Floor-level shower drainage is central to the announced direction toward accessible, low-profile systems, so any weak early results would be attributed to the start-up phase.
The designer drain has a dedicated page and embodies the firm's design-quality claim, so public commitment and fit argue for keeping it.
The shower element with integrated slope fits the integrated, renovation-oriented direction, and after only one year management would see disappointing results as temporary.
The backflow-protected basement drain is less central to bathroom design, but its own page and the investment already made favor persistence.
The air-admittance valve is a peripheral accessory that is only mentioned on the website, making it the most likely to be cut, though as a complement to the system it is still likely kept.
